The allegation against the petitioners is that the disputed land stood recorded in the name of Sukan Ram.
The complainant claims to be a descendant of Sukan Ram through her marriage with her husband Binod Ram.
It is alleged that the complainant entered into an agreement with Ramesh Oraon and Md. Azad.
Ramesh Oraon and Md. Azad entered into an agreement with Zafar Alam.
Zafar Alam sold the land of the complainant to the petitioner No.1 namely Pramod Kumar Pal, who is the accused No.3 of the complaint.
When the complainant asked the co-accused Zafar Alam that the land belongs to her, Zafar Alam abused the complainant.
The petitioner-accused persons of the case have cheated the complainant; as the petitioners in criminal conspiracy with the co-accused person have executed the sale deed.

The specific allegation against the petitioner No.1, who is the accused No.3 of the complainant, is that, he executed the sale deed, in criminal conspiracy with the co-accused person and the petitioner No.2 Pramod Kumar Pal claimed himself to be the grand-son of Sukan Ram and by such misrepresentation executed sale deed No.1320 dated 28.02.2022.

It is alleged that the petitioners in criminal conspiracy with the co- accused persons have created forged sale deed; on the basis of the forged khatian and forged land revenue receipt, issued by the Circle Office, and on the basis of such forged documents, the petitioners have sold the land belonging to the complainant bearing khata No.186, plot No.719, Thana No.205, Mauja Ranchi.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners draws attention of this Court to Annexure-4 which is the decree of Title Suit No.85 of 1972 of the court of Sub- Ordinate Judge-VI, Ranchi and submits that in that suit it has categorically been mentioned that the defendant No.12 namely Jugal Kishore Prasad was the son of Sukan Ram and the petitioner No.1 is the son of Jugal Kishore Prasad.
Similarly, the petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of Jayant Lal Pal who is the defendant No.8 of the said Title Suit No.85 of 1972.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners next submits that the allegations against the petitioners are false.

The land in respect of which the petitioners have executed the sale deed is the ancestral land of the petitioners and the ancestors of the petitioners include Sukan Ram, who admittedly by the complainant, is the owner of the land.
It is then submitted that the Title Suit No.85 of 1972 was a partition suit between the heirs of original owner namely Sukan Ram and Dukhan Ram.
But the learned court dismissed the suit instituted by the heirs of Dukhan Ram as inter alia
the plot No.1225 belongs to the heirs of Sukan Ram, who have been arrayed as defendant Nos.8 and 12.

It is further submitted that the complainant is an imposter, who in connivance with the land brokers is in the habit of creating false and fabricated documents for wrecking vengeance upon innocent persons, like the petitioners.
It is also submitted that on earlier occasion, Complaint Case No. 734 of 2020 was instituted by the complainant in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi.

Upon being referred to police, Hindpidi P.S. Case No.149 of 2020 was registered on the basis of similar versions and narrations with respect to the property sold from khata No.186 and the complainant has deliberately suppressed about the said complaint, while instituting the present complaint and on this score alone the entire criminal proceeding is to be quashed and set aside.

In this respect, the learned counsel for the petitioner relies upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Krishna Pramod Kumar Pal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104909177/

It therefore remains to be seen whether the claim of the complainant that the execution of sale deeds by the first accused, who was in no way connected with the land, amounted to committing forgery of the documents with the intention of taking possession of the complainant's land (and that Accused 2 to 5 as the purchaser, witness, scribe and stamp vendor,

Therefore, execution of such document (purporting to convey some property of which he is not the owner) is not execution of a false document as defined under Section 464 of the Code.
If what is executed is not a false document, there is no forgery.
If there is no forgery, then neither Section 467 nor Section 471 of the Code are attracted."

7. It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the complainant in her statement on solemn affirmation has given inter alia a different picture from the allegations made in the complaint.

Hence, it is submitted that even if the entire allegations made against the petitioners are considered to be true in their entirety, no offence in respect of which prima facie case has been found by the learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class-VI, Ranchi, is made out against the petitioners.

It is also submitted that in the absence of any allegation of cheating and thereby inducing delivery of any property against the petitioners, the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code is not made out against the petitioners.
Hence, it is submitted that the prayer as prayed for in this Criminal Miscellaneous Petition be allowed.

Learned Addl.P.P. appearing for the State and the learned senior counsel for the opposite party No.2 on the other hand vehemently oppose the prayer of the petitioners made in this Criminal Miscellaneous Petition and submit that the allegation made against the petitioners is sufficient to constitute the offence in respect of which the learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class-VI, Ranchi has found prima facie case against the petitioners.
Hence, it is submitted that this Criminal Miscellaneous Petition, being without any merit, be dismissed.

So far as the offence punishable under Section 406 of the Indian Penal Code is concerned, the essential ingredients to constitute the offence punishable under Section 406 of the Indian Penal Code are that:-

(v) The accused dishonestly used or disposed of that property or willfully suffered any other person to do so in failure of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or any legal contract touching upon discharge of such trust.

Hence, this Court is of the considered view that the dispute between the parties is at best a civil dispute and a cloak of criminal case has been given to the civil dispute for the purpose of wrecking vengeance, which practice has been deprecated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in several judgments.

Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that even if the entire allegations made against the petitioners are considered to be true in their entirety, still none of the offences punishable under Sections 467, 468, 471 of the Indian Penal Code is made out against the petitioners.

So far as the offence punishable under Section 504 of the Indian Penal Code is concerned, the essential ingredients to constitute the offence punishable under Section 504 of the Indian Penal Code is that:-
